messages:
morgan.support: Heads-up 4: customer disputes invoice; says client-side estimator reports ~900 tokens but invoice shows ~1,150. They included system prompt, multiple short user messages (batched), and one function call that returns a ~3k-char JSON blob.

devin.eng: Can you paste a sanitized request + the usage block from the API? Also which SDK and version is the customer using?

morgan.support: They sent this minimal payload (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-1.5\",
  \"messages\": [
    {\"role\":\"system\",\"content\":\"You are precise and brief.\"},
    {\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Explain X in one paragraph.\"},
    {\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Add a short example.\"}
  ],
  \"functions\": [{\"name\":\"fetch-db\",\"parameters\":{}}]
}
```
API returned:
```
{\"id\":\"cmpl-abc\",\"usage\":{\"prompt_tokens\":940,\"completion_tokens\":210,\"total_tokens\":1150},\"choices\":[{\"message\":{\"role\":\"assistant\",\"content\":\"{\\n  \\\"result\\\": \\\"...long json...\\\n}\"}}]}
```
Customer claims their estimator (Node SDK) returns 900 tokens.

oscar.billing: Ticket opened BLG-9987 and flagged billing review. Pls attach request id + invoice lines.

devin.eng: Quick hypotheses: (1) SDK estimator may not include role-separator tokens or function-return framing; (2) batching concatenation and message framing differences; (3) streaming/truncation handling if function returned large content in multiple chunks. Which SDK?

morgan.support: Node SDK v0.12.1. They ran estimator like: `sdk.tokens.estimate({messages})` and got 900. They said they do include system in that call.

emma.sre: I pulled logs using req id rq_03Cxy9. Server tokenizer shows 1150 total. I reran a local server-side tokenization of the exact bytes we stored and matched invoice. Ran the v0.12.1 estimator binary and reproduced ~900.

devin.eng: Interesting. I made a local reproducer that includes the function response (returned as assistant content after tool execution). Two important differences we found: (A) our server treats the function-returned text as part of the prompt for subsequent handling and counts framing tokens for the function/assistant roles; (B) the SDK v0.12 token estimator skips counting function->assistant framing and collapses separators when batching. For many small batched user messages this can shave off a consistent ~6-12 tokens per message which multiplies.

morgan.support: Customer also mentioned they use emojis and some non-ascii chars in examples. Could that explain the delta?

devin.eng: Could be small part. There was an earlier SDK bug where multi-byte UTF-8 sequences were sometimes normalized differently; patch was included in v0.13.0. But the main delta here is framing and function return accounting.

oscar.billing: Billing: please hold on credits until we confirm reproducible cause. If it's an SDK bug and we confirm >10% mismatch, ops recommends a partial credit.

devin.eng: Reproducer results:
- server tokenizer (exact serialized messages we send): total 1150
- node-sdk v0.12.1 estimator: total 902
- node-sdk v0.13.0 estimator: total 1146
So v0.13 aligns closely.

morgan.support: Can we provide a short-term workaround for customer who can't upgrade?

devin.eng: Two options: (1) call our tokenization endpoint `/v1/tokenize` with the exact serialized messages payload they intend to send; that will return server-token counts and is safe to use without changing production logic, or (2) patch their local estimator by serializing messages exactly like the SDK does in v0.13 (include role separator tokens and include function return roles)  I'll paste a minimal JS snippet for workaround:
```
// quick tokenization call
const serverCount = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tokenize', {method:'POST', body: JSON.stringify({messages})});
console.log(await serverCount.json());
```
Option (1) is lower-risk.

billing-ops: Pre-approve up to $400 credit pending eng confirmation + customer verification. Provide invoice lines and time ranges.

morgan.support: I told the customer: try v0.13.0 in a staging environment or use the tokenize endpoint. They're hesitant to upgrade in prod mid-cycle. They asked if we can run a retrospective tokenization over their archived requests to estimate the overcharge.

devin.eng: We can run a one-off tokenization job if they provide a list of request payloads or request ids. Will need explicit consent. It'll cost us some compute but useful for reconciliation.

oscar.billing: Provide the request ids and invoice window, we'll correlate and hold credits if validated.

devin.eng: Created PR internal: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/pull/512 which changes estimator default to include system+functions and adds an `include_system_and_functions` flag for backwards compatibility. Tests added.

morgan.support: Great. I'll update the ticket BLG-9987 with repro, suggested workaround, and ask for request list for backfill. Customer asked for rough timeline  can we turn around tokenization of ~3k archived requests in 48-72hrs?

devin.eng: Yes, estimate 24-48hrs to run tokenize job if they provide payloads. Emma (SRE) will help with job.

emma.sre: I can schedule. Please collect sanitized payloads + request ids. Also note: normalize newlines consistently before tokenizing (we saw \r\n vs \n differences change counts by 1-2 tokens per message).

morgan.support: Thanks team. Billing locked credit hold and eng will do verification. I'll push the customer to staging test v0.13 first.

token-bot: Ticket BLG-9987 updated: status -> triaged, assignee -> devin.eng, notes -> potential SDK estimator undercount (fix in v0.13).

oscar.billing: We'll wait for eng's tokenization run and customer confirmation before finalizing credits.

morgan.support: Closing the thread for now; will reopen if customer provides more payloads or rejects upgrade.
